comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find claims C1, C21-C27 regarding iNKT cell metabolic profile (favoring fatty acid synthesis over glycolysis) to be well-supported. OpenEval cites specific figures while peer reviewers describe results as 'clearcut and logically presented.'

Complete agreement. Both find claims C42-C43 regarding α-GalCer model validation supported. OpenEval provides detailed figure references while peer reviewers accept this as confirmatory evidence without explicit discussion.

Full agreement. Both find claims C46-C52 regarding cell-intrinsic effects and developmental impacts supported. OpenEval emphasizes mixed chimera experiments while peer reviewers acknowledge 'bone marrow chimera studies' as part of the comprehensive approach.

Agreement on claims C87-C89 ruling out epigenetic mechanisms. Both find the negative control experiments (methylation and HDAC inhibitor studies) support the proposed mechanism, though peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss these details.

Divergent evaluations of claims C8-C9, C98-C102, C115 regarding human relevance. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to limited sample size (n=10), lack of functional validation, and inability to establish causality. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with editor noting human data 'adds compelling evidence.' This represents the most significant disagreement.

Strong agreement on claims C53-C64 regarding metabolic reprogramming and glycolysis-cell death link. OpenEval provides detailed figure-by-figure analysis while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic connection without challenge. Peer review also includes C5-C7 not in OpenEval R6.

Agreement on claims C4, C44-C45, C90-C91 regarding adoptive transfer experiments demonstrating ACC1's cell-intrinsic role. Both find evidence strong. Peer R3 also covers C92-C93 (rescue experiments) which OpenEval addresses separately in R10.

Agreement on claims C73-C86 regarding the ACC1-FABP-PPARγ signaling axis. Both find the mechanistic pathway supported. OpenEval notes that direct palmitate measurement would strengthen conclusions, while peer reviewers accept the logic without this caveat. OpenEval R8 includes additional claims (C72, C104, C113) not in peer R6.

Agreement on claims C2-C3, C28-C33, C38 regarding ACC1-deficient mice failing to develop asthma in OVA and HDM models. Both find evidence well-supported across multiple models. Peer R2 covers subset of claims from OpenEval R2.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R2 addresses claims C34-C41 regarding reduced iNKT cells and altered gene expression, which peer R4 confirms regarding cytokine secretion and cell-type specificity. Both find evidence supported.

Partial agreement on claims C94-C95 regarding in vivo metabolic phenotype restoration. Both find evidence supported. OpenEval R10 also covers C92-C93 (addressed in peer R3) while peer R11 includes C96-C97 (addressed in OpenEval R11 and R13).

Agreement on claims C65-C71 regarding PPARγ downregulation and pioglitazone rescue. Both find evidence supported. OpenEval R7 also includes C111 not in peer R6, while peer R6 covers broader mechanistic pathway claims.
Agreement on claim C96 regarding chemokine receptor expression ruling out trafficking defects. Both find this supported as part of comprehensive mechanistic characterization.

Agreement on claims C92-C93 regarding rescue experiments with palmitate/pioglitazone. Both find these strongly supported. Peer R3 explicitly notes 'authors were able to reverse the phenotype with PPARγ agonist.'

Minimal overlap on claim C97. Both find integrative conclusions supported. OpenEval R13 covers broader set of summary claims (C103, C105, C110, C114, C117) while peer R11 focuses on specific in vivo findings.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background/context claims C10-C20 as supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers do not typically assess background knowledge claims.
OpenEval R15 evaluates literature contextualization claims C106-C107, C112, C116 as appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R16 evaluates claims C108-C109 regarding metabolic effects on survival and effector functions as supported by 2-DG and adoptive transfer experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific integrative claims.
